title: How to create 3D models with ChatGPT
summary: ChatGPT can create and edit 3D models and scenes with the Spline plugin. How to use it in ChatGPT and Codex, and how to pick GPT-6.2 Astra or GPT-6.2 Sol inside Spline.
body_markdown:
ChatGPT can create 3D models and scenes, and edit them, with the Spline plugin. Ask for a scene and ChatGPT builds it in a real Spline file, with objects, materials, lighting, animation and interactions, that opens in a panel beside the chat. You can also go the other way: pick OpenAI's GPT models inside Spline's own AI Agent. This guide covers ChatGPT, Codex and the GPT models in Spline, and how they compare with other models in[Spline Arena](https://spline.design/arena) .


Built in Spline with OpenAI's GPT models: Duo, DualSense and The Plaza


## Create 3D models in ChatGPT


The Spline plugin connects ChatGPT to Spline. There's nothing to install and no API key:


1. Add the Spline plugin


Open the[Spline plugin in ChatGPT's plugin directory](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/spline) and add it. The first time you use it, sign in with your Spline account and allow access.


2. Describe the 3D scene


Ask for what you want, like "a 3D chair configurator with buttons that switch the fabric color". ChatGPT builds it in a new Spline file, and the Spline editor opens in a panel next to the conversation.


3. Refine it, then publish


Keep asking for changes, or move things yourself in the panel: ChatGPT reads the file again before its next edit. When it's ready, ask ChatGPT to publish it, and it hands back a link to share or embed.


ChatGPT can also open a Spline file you already have from the panel and edit it, generate 3D models and images with Spline AI, and design 2D screens in Hana. More in[Introducing Spline for ChatGPT](https://spline.design/blog/introducing-spline-for-chatgpt) and the[docs](https://docs.spline.design/generate/plugins/chatgpt) .


## Create 3D with Codex


The same plugin works in Codex. Add it from the[plugin directory](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/spline) , or add only the Spline MCP server with` codex mcp add spline --url https://mcp.spline.design/mcp` and sign in with` codex mcp login spline` .


Codex can then build a scene in Spline and put it into your project: ask it to publish the scene, and it hands back the public URL, a Spline Viewer embed or a code export for React, Next.js, Vanilla JS, three.js or react-three-fiber, and wires it in. Publishing again updates the same link, so your site picks up scene changes without a code change.


## Use GPT models inside Spline


Spline's AI Agent offers two OpenAI models, each as a tier in its model picker:


- Astra


GPT-6.2 Astra


OpenAI's flagship, and one of the quickest builders in Spline Arena


- Medium


GPT-6.2 Sol


Rates level with Astra, for about a third of the cost per scene


In the 3D editor, open the **Agent** tab at the top of the left sidebar. At the bottom of the panel, next to the prompt box, pick **Astra** or **Medium** in the model picker, and an **effort** level, from Low to Max: how much the model thinks before it acts. High is enough for most scenes; go higher for interactions, physics or games.


Then describe the scene and press Enter. The Agent builds it with the editor's own tools, so every change is a normal edit you can undo, adjust by hand or keep prompting on. Hana's AI Agent has the same pickers.


- **Astra (GPT-6.2 Astra)** when time matters: it builds a scene in a few minutes, about four times faster than Claude Fable 5.2.
- **Medium (GPT-6.2 Sol)** rates about the same as Astra for about a third of the cost per scene. A good default for most work.


In[Spline Arena](https://spline.design/arena) , where people vote on scenes without knowing which model made them, both GPT-6.2 models opened in the top six when they joined, almost level with each other: Astra builds faster, Sol costs less. How every model compares is in[Designing with 3D AI agents](https://spline.design/blog/3d-ai-agents) and the live[Rankings](https://app.spline.design/arena/rankings) .


## FAQ


### Can ChatGPT create 3D models?


Yes. With the Spline plugin, ChatGPT builds 3D models and scenes you can edit: shapes, materials, lighting, animation and interactions. They're saved as Spline files, and you can export them as GLB, USDZ or STL (for 3D printing), or publish them to the web.


### Can ChatGPT edit 3D models?


Yes. Open a Spline file from the plugin's panel and ask for changes. ChatGPT reads the scene before it edits, so it builds on what's there, including changes you made by hand.


### Is there a ChatGPT plugin for 3D modeling?


Yes,[Spline](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/spline) , in ChatGPT's plugin directory. It works in Codex too.


### Is it free?


The plugin works on every Spline plan, including Free. Each Spline action ChatGPT takes counts toward your plan's MCP tool call limits; see[pricing](https://spline.design/pricing) . Inside Spline, the AI Agent runs on the AI credits included with paid plans.


### Which GPT model is best for 3D in Spline?


In Spline Arena, GPT-6.2 Sol and GPT-6.2 Astra rate almost level, both in the top six. Astra builds faster, and Sol costs about a third as much per scene. The[Rankings](https://app.spline.design/arena/rankings) have the current standings for every model.
